title: Vain Are the Hopes the Sons of Men
description: Vain Are the Hopes the Sons of Men in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 94, headed “Justification by faith, not by works; or, The law condemns, grace justifies, Rom. 3. 19-22”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Vain are the hopes the sons of men On their own works have built; Their hearts by na-ture all un-clean, And all their ac-tions guilt.

lines: Vain are the hopes the sons of men
On their own works have built;
Their hearts by nature all unclean,
Let Jew and Gentile stop their mouths
And the whole race of Adam stand
In vain we ask God's righteous law
Since to convince and to condemn
Is all the law can do.
Jesus, how glorious is thy grace,
When in thy name we trust,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
